answer: An agent marketplace for a summit makes a bonded registry the only inlet for new sellers: each identity must lock $100 for 30 days before bidding, and proven non-delivery forfeits its bond. Viewed through the prism of capital costs, 1,000 fake sellers require $100,000 locked at once. Splitting funds among aliases cannot multiply bidding access; the attacker must supply fresh collateral for each identity and risks losing it when cheating is proved.
